label: late-episode update-gate drop, deeper when policy favours a1 / after a1 S2 u
explanation: Raw z of unit 20 stays near 1 (saturated) for most of the episode. In the last ~20 trials it falls, most at D2, then GO, and least at D1. Timing alone gives R^2 0.58. The part beyond timing has three pieces. (1) A steeper within-decile ramp late in the episode, max(ep_trial-80,0)^2 per phase. (2) A late-episode interaction with the model policy logit(a1)-logit(a2): the more the policy favours a1, the lower z, strongest at D2. This is a model-internal quantity, not a future one. (3) Two history/choice effects that do not depend on episode time: z is lower at GO and D2 after a1 S2 unrewarded (about -0.06), and higher at D2 after choosing a2 than a1. Reward of the trial before, value, and the hidden good state add little; the good-state residual is mostly the choice effect. An observed-only version that replaces the policy logit with the action and the previous action scored dev 0.46. The 8 terms score dev 0.55 and test 0.57 beyond timing. This is above the additive all ceiling of 0.33 because the late-episode interactions are outside that ceiling. Many large residuals at t90-99 are left unexplained and look like episode-level variation.

issues: The original 8 terms reproduce as claimed: 0.568 test R^2 beyond timing. Timing alone gives 0.578.

The 'finer timing ramp' caveat is overstated. The three max(ep_trial-80,0)^2 ramps on their own add only 0.020 beyond timing on test. Nearly all the gain comes from the late x policy-logit interaction: ramps plus late*choice give 0.478. Without the late weighting, choice gives only 0.222. So the policy claim holds.

A systematic gap was missed: a late-episode drop at GO after any unrewarded previous trial. Adding late*(GO)*(prev_reward==0) and late*(D2)*(prev_reward==0) raises the score from 0.478 to 0.553 (test). With the best 8-term set, the GO-unrewarded weight is -0.013 per trial past 80, about -0.25 by trial 99, and the generic GO ramp weight falls to about 0. The late GO drop is therefore mostly an 'after no reward' drop, not a pure timing ramp. The explanation's claim that the 'reward of the trial before adds little' is wrong for the previous trial's reward at GO.

Misses on the original terms point to the same gap. The most over-predicted cells are GO after a2 S2 u (-0.027), GO after a1 S2 u (-0.027) and GO after a1 S1 u (-0.019). The most under-predicted are GO after a2 S1 r, a1 S1 r and a2 S2 r (+0.018, +0.017, +0.013). The profile residuals also show that GO after any unrewarded trial is lower and after any rewarded trial is higher, so the effect is not specific to a1 S2 u.

The a1 S2 u effect checks out. It does not depend on episode time: a flat term gives 0.568 and a late-weighted one 0.561. It still holds (weight -0.056) after adding the general late-unrewarded terms. The D2 action effect also holds: dropping it lowers test R^2 to 0.526.

Large window-level misses at trials 90-99 remain in both term sets: GO actual 0.2-0.3 against predicted 0.6-0.7, and D1 actual 0.5-0.7 against predicted about 0.93. These look like episode-level variation that none of the variables capture, so confidence should stay medium.
